cells.normalized_text: Upon emptying the Magazine: Refills 60% ↑70% of all damage instances scored. Always rounds up. Counter persists through stow. Requires shooting at least 28.5% of the Magazine Capacity for refill to activate. Always rounds up. Hits within 1? seconds of triggering the refill do not count. Displayed by the active buff indicator. Adaptive Burst Linear Fusion Rifle Behavior: Counts each bolt individually. Refill Amount is 14% of damage instances scored.

Reload Perk Notes: Generate = Grants Ammo to Magazine out of thin air, up to its Base Magazine Size. Does not work with Overflown Magazines. Overflow = Increases Base Magazine Capacity by a certain amount, rounded up. Refill = Reload, but does not have an animation and doesn't proc on-reload perks. Pulls from reserves on Special and Power Weapons. For Heat Weapons, it will instead be "Dissipates X Heat" to discern it from manual venting Reload = Procs on-reload perks. Manual Reload, Marksman's Dodge, and Dragon's Shadow all count as regular reloads. For Heat Weapons, finishing a manual vent will count as a regular reload.

Post-proc suppression remains 1? second. Adaptive Burst LFR counts each bolt; enhanced rate 16.33% is explicitly provisional.

engine_foundation: Accepted fire exposes immutable before_magazine, magazine, capacity and unmodified_capacity, all in rounds. Zero-cost fire and rejected requests are distinguishable from a paid emptying transition.

Accepted fire and ShotGroups progress/summary expose origin_source while preserving their distinct shot references. Multiple groups may share an origin; one complete group is not proof that every group from that fire has ended.

Set membership conditions can correlate remembered event identities within the declared buff instance. A victim snapshot captures the identity while querying victim membership at impact. Source membership freezes at use.
The data rules below compose these primitives without adding perk-specific Java. Original-game settlement timing remains uncalibrated.
remaining_requirements: Resolve 28.5 versus 28.75 percent firing threshold, measure post-proc suppression and verify the provisional enhanced Adaptive Burst rate.
Calibrate emptying and group settlement timing, final misses, overlapping triggers, delayed explosions, reload/proc resets, zero-transfer and other ammo-perk interactions in the original game.

Calibrate damage-instance eligibility, immunity/blockage, indirect perk damage, repeated contacts, Divinity cage and special exotic/heat weapons; the current explicit credit policy is not a complete original-game hit taxonomy.
Bind each production weapon to its exact actual group count and sufficient settlement window; no universal inferred group count is provided.
Complete formal weapon/subclass/content catalog assembly, hot-swap/death/offline policies, visual assets/HUD and physical-weapon/projectile restart acceptance.

required_source_parameters.minimum_fired_fraction: multiplier; explicit choice between conflicting observations
required_source_parameters.adaptive_fraction: multiplier; explicit per-variant choice, used only by Adaptive Burst source tag
required_source_parameters.groups: positive integer count; exact settlement groups emitted by the weapon for an accepted trigger
required_source_parameters.settlement_seconds: positive seconds; must accommodate the declared grouped attack
required_source_parameters.receipt_seconds: positive seconds; event identity retention policy, not a gameplay loop limit

content_policies: Each current perk source matches accepted owner and weapon. Paid accepted round costs accumulate; generic ammo spends, rejected fire and zero-cost fire do not create emptying transitions. Threshold uses the accepted effective capacity, exact decimal multiplication and ceiling.

Applied weapon-credited damage instances increment hits, including explicitly weapon-credited indirect perk damage. Unique damage_id receipts are counted, not unique pellet/target pairs. Immune, blocked, cancelled, failed and wrong-owner/weapon facts are excluded.

Damage and accepted-fire identities are remembered for receipt_seconds. Ignored-window hits are also remembered so replay after the window cannot count. Per-entry cleanup is source-owned; stow preserves counters, source detachment clears private state and cancels cleanup.

Paid emptying remembers origin_source and the declared group count. A later paid emptying replaces this pending candidate. Unique group shot IDs accumulate results; only the final expected result can settle, and every result must be complete. Missing or incomplete groups never invent hits or a refill.

The pending candidate has an explicit finite timeout. Group completion is a Chorus policy, not established original-game projectile timing. Earlier in-flight triggers are not implicitly awaited; hits are attributed to the counter active when their facts are processed.

Settlement requires the current magazine still be empty, enough paid rounds and a positive hit count. Other refill/generation filling the magazine cancels this candidate without erasing the hit/fired ledger.

Ordinary/enhanced refill is ceil(hits * 0.6/0.7). Adaptive Burst uses its explicit variant coefficient and every qualified bolt damage instance. Refill uses current base capacity and that weapon reserve, never changes base capacity and emits no ordinary reload completion.

A positive transfer clears hit/fired counters and grants the configured finite suppression window. Zero transfer clears only the pending candidate; no proc, suppression or immediate replay on later reserve gain is inferred.

Qualified reload_finished clears counters and pending candidate, while retaining duplicate receipts and any active suppression. Late hits after reload use the new processing-time ledger. Real manual reload is tested; ability reload producers and edge timing still require composition tests.
Checkpoint round-trip restores pure counters, pending group identities and cooldown without reissuing a transfer. Physical live projectiles across a process restart are not covered by this test.
Unknown damage or post-transfer world results preserve committed facts and stop execution; they cannot infer a successful missing hit, refund ammunition or replay a refill.
